title: Filter with a boolean mask
summary: A boolean mask is a list of true-or-false choices. True positions are kept when used to select array values.
introduction: A boolean mask is a list of true-or-false choices. True positions are kept when used to select array values. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Explain filter with a boolean mask
Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A boolean mask is a list of true-or-false choices. True positions are kept when used to select array values.

blocks.code:
import numpy as np

scores = np.array([3, 8, 5])
mask = scores >= 5
print(scores[mask].tolist())
blocks.title: Filter with a boolean mask

blocks.text: The output is [8, 5]. The comparison keeps scores of at least 5.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Use element-wise logical operators carefully; normal Python and/or do not combine whole array masks.
For more detail later, use this [NumPy further reading](https://numpy.org/doc/stable/user/absolute_beginners.html).
